messages:
sam_support: FYI we got a ticket — customer says their org's Usage & Cost dashboard is missing data for non-admin users for the past 90 days. Admins see full history.

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the customer's org id and an example user role that can't see the data? Also which dashboard(s)?

sam_support: Org `org_5543`, dashboard: `Billing → Usage by Route`, affected roles: `team_viewer`, `analyst-readonly` (non-admin). Customer says admins see everything. They provided a screenshot where charts are empty and a tooltip says "no data for selected range".

alex_support: Repro steps requested to customer: (1) login as non-admin role → (2) open Billing → Usage by Route → (3) set range 90d. They confirmed and said page loads but panels empty.

ben_sre: Can you ask them to run the internal analytics API query and paste response? Quick check: `GET /internal/analytics/orgs/org_5543/usage?range=90d` (needs internal token). If empty for non-admin but populated for admin, likely an ACL/filter applied at aggregation layer. :eyes:

sam_support: Customer sent the API output for a non-admin token — here's the snippet: ```json
{"status":"ok","data":[],"note":"filtered_by_role"}
```

alex_support: Ok that `filtered_by_role` tag is new. pinging @ben_sre and @maria_product to check retention/acl changes rolled this week.

maria_product: We shipped a minor change to retention/visibility on 2026-03-10 — it should be backwards compatible but I see a config flag `role_to_retention_map` was updated. @pm_elena do you recall any deliberate mapping for hyphenated/underscore roles?

pm_elena: We intended to map any role to one of `admin|analytics_reader|viewer`. Looks like the mapping service normalizes names but a recent regex change excluded roles with a hyphen. Filing as regression.

ben_sre: Digging into logs — aggregation service added an ACL clause when building the query: `AND role in (:allowed_roles)` and the allowed_roles list came back empty for `team_viewer` because of the mapping miss. That explains empty arrays. I can backfill allowed_roles for affected orgs as a short-term fix.

analytics_bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0311-03 — scope: analytics visibility. Affected orgs count: 18. Potential root cause: role mapping regex regression in `service-config` v2.9.1.

alex_support: Proposed immediate mitigations to offer customer: (A) grant `analytics_reader` to the affected users/org (temporary), (B) we backfill allowed_roles and re-run aggregation job, (C) full rollback of `service-config` to v2.9.0 if needed. Which do you recommend, @ben_sre?

ben_sre: Do (B) + (A) for fastest customer unblock. I'll run a targeted ACL backfill for `org_5543` now and patch the mapping service. After backfill, aggregation should return data; dashboards will refresh within ~10-20m. If anything persists, we'll roll back.

maria_product: Patch PR opened: #5487 — fixes regex and adds unit test for hyphenated roles. Targeted deploy in 15m.

ben_sre: Backfill job kicked: `job_id=bf-20260311-233` — reindexing aggregates for affected orgs. For `org_5543` progress: 0% -> 60% -> 100%. Verified via `SELECT count(*) FROM aggregates WHERE org_id='org_5543' AND window='90d'` returned expected rows.

alex_support: Customer notified: "We're applying a fix that will restore visibility for non-admin roles within ~20 minutes. We'll follow up when everything is confirmed." :thumbsup:

sam_support: Customer replied: "Thanks, Alex. We're team are unblocked now — charts reappeared for our analysts. Please let us know when fix is permanent."

ben_sre: Patch deployed to prod and config fixed. I'll keep the backfill monitoring for 2 hours. Postmortem will include why mapping regression wasn't caught by CI.

maria_product: Note for postmortem: add a rule to prevent silent empty `allowed_roles` lists — fail fast. Also add an integration test that runs a simulated non-admin query.

alex_support: Closing loop with customer and offering a 1:1 runthrough of RBAC/roles if they want.

sam_support: Customer asked for timeline for postmortem — told them we'll share RCA within 48 hours.

ben_sre: Incident resolved; marks: :white_check_mark:.
